blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Typhoon Rosal has slowed down and may continue to weaken into a severe tropical storm by Saturday, Oct. 24, the state weather bureau said. A Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) weather specialist, John Manalo, said in Pagasa’s 5 p.m. weather advisory that Rosal’s movement had slowed from 25 kilometers per hour to 15 kph. As of 3 p.m., the typhoon was located 360 km east of Itbayat, Batanes, within the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR).
